system.name: MuxWise
system.one_liner: an LLM serving framework using intra-GPU prefill-decode multiplexing to meet SLOs at high goodput

components.name: Contention-tolerant estimator
components.role: provides worst-case latency estimates by combining a solo-run predictor with a contention guard, built from offline profiling

components.name: Solo-run predictor
components.role: predicts a request's latency executing alone

components.name: Contention guard
components.role: adjusts the latency estimate to account for contention from concurrently multiplexed prefill/decode work

components.name: One-time offline profiling
components.role: offline profiling run per LLM/hardware pair that supplies data to the predictor and contention guard

components.name: SLO-aware dispatcher
components.role: uses estimator latency to schedule prefill layers and decode iterations, producing a multiplexing plan (SM/block partition)

components.name: Bubble-less multiplex engine
components.role: executes prefill layers (PLs) and decode (D) concurrently on the GPU without pipeline bubbles, per the dispatcher's plan

flows.what: multiplexing plan (P: X SMs/Y Blocks, D: Z SMs)
runtime execution feedback updating the contention guard

content.key_idea: MuxWise combines an offline-profiled, contention-tolerant latency estimator with an SLO-aware dispatcher that computes an SM/block multiplexing plan, driving a bubble-less engine that runs layer-wise prefill and decode concurrently on the same GPU.
content.reading_order: Clockwise from top: offline profiling feeds the contention-tolerant estimator, which sends a latency estimate down to the SLO-aware dispatcher; the dispatcher's plan drives the bubble-less multiplex engine, which updates the estimator's contention guard at runtime.

summary: MuxWise is an LLM serving framework that adopts intra-GPU prefill-decode (PD) multiplexing to meet per-request SLOs while maximizing goodput. This figure gives MuxWise's architecture overview as three cooperating boxes. The Contention-tolerant estimator (top), built from one-time offline profiling, combines a Solo-run predictor with a Contention guard to output worst-case latency estimates. These estimates flow to the SLO-aware dispatcher (bottom left), which computes a multiplexing plan partitioning GPU SMs/blocks between prefill (P) and decode (D) work. That plan drives the Bubble-less multiplex engine (bottom right), whose small timeline diagram shows prefill layers (PLs) and decode (D) micro-batches executing concurrently with partition boundaries, inflight batches, and sync points, while runtime feedback updates the contention guard. Cyan, cream, and blue-purple fills distinguish the three subsystems and their inner components, and red arrows/labels (Latency, Plan, Update) trace the control loop between them.
